entity.name: Deepak Ezhumalai
entity.description:
Independent machine-learning researcher in Chennai, India. I work in the open: pre-registered experiments, released code and models, and negative results reported alongside positive ones.

Since November 2026 I have contributed cross-scroll ink detection to ScrollPrize/villa, the open-source (MIT) toolkit of the Vesuvius Challenge, which reads carbonised Herculaneum papyrus scrolls from X-ray CT scans. Pull request ScrollPrize/villa#2512 adds a scan-type conversion for training, a self-training command and their tests and documentation. I published the checkpoints on Hugging Face under CC BY-NC 4.0, the licence of the training data.

Other public work: VersionOutcomes (Apache-2.0), a benchmark of real before/after outcomes of Python function calls across library commits, and an analysis of ARC-AGI-3 agent results. Code: https://github.com/DeepakEz

projects.name: Cross-scroll ink detection for the Vesuvius Challenge toolkit (villa)
projects.description:
Ink-detection models for the Herculaneum scrolls work well on the scroll they were trained on and much worse on a new one. The scrolls still unread were scanned natively, while most labelled 9 um training data are renders pooled from finer scans. My contribution to villa targets that gap.

What exists today:
- A fitted pooled-to-native scan conversion applied during training. With PHerc 0139 held out of fitting and training, it raised native ROC-AUC there by +0.024 without mirror inference and +0.011 with it, across three matched seeds.
- A self-training command using confidence-filtered pseudo-labels. It added +0.018 ROC-AUC with mirror inference on segments excluded from adaptation (three seeds, 13 of 15 segment-seed pairs).
- Released checkpoints, configs and model cards on Hugging Face.
- Outside use: another participant ran the released scan-conversion checkpoint on PHerc 1447 w060, a scroll I never used, and the gain repeated (0.711 vs 0.672-0.687 for three baseline seeds).

Limits, stated plainly: the pull request is open, not merged. On PHerc 1447 a different public reader (v8-in) still scores higher (0.804). My models do not yet make letters readable on unread scrolls.

plans.name: Maintainer time, six months
plans.description: Rs 40,000 per month for six months of part-time work (about 20 hours a week) on the milestones below, paid in quarterly tranches. Q1 (months 1-3): M1, turn PR #2512 into reviewable upstream changes (address reviewer feedback, split scan conversion and self-training into separate PRs with tests, report adapted and unadapted segments separately). M2, release a reproducible leave-one-scroll-out ink benchmark script with results for every scroll that has verified labels (PHerc 0139, 1447, 0841, 0343P), including public readers that beat mine. Q2 (months 4-6): M3, test whether the scan conversion helps the stronger 8 um model family, and release checkpoints and model cards whichever way it comes out. M4, a tutorial that reproduces the cross-scroll result on one 16 GB consumer GPU. Each quarter: a public progress update on the FOSS United forum; at least one talk at a FOSS United meetup.
